verdict:
VIOLATIONS FOUND — the design breaches the SCOPE fence in three distinct ways and contradicts itself on the boundary at least six times. Twenty-two findings, nineteen structural.

**The fence is not actually closed.** Three separate items schedule production work inside an architecture-only cycle: the migration map's Phase 1 enters "immediately, in parallel with Phase 0" and rewrites live bot copy, Telegram replies and the AI chat's gift offer; §7.1 authorises probing owner/staff commands in production on a read-only classification the probe itself is meant to establish; and Wave 1 ships compiled TypeScript into the deployed backend artefact plus a build-gating CI job, with the fence redefined from "0 runtime changes" to "no reachable runtime code" and then restated as "nothing in production has changed". The packages plan places the same Phase-1 work in Waves 5 and 6 behind a human-approved gate, so the two normative documents disagree about whether production may be touched this week.

**Two deletions are authorised outside the only gate that may authorise one.** `localStorage.me_is_staff` is marked "DELETE FIRST, UNCONDITIONALLY, NO PARITY GATE" and the B2 fenced Telegram entry points are "retire immediately" — both in documents that open by saying nothing they contain authorises a deletion, and the second ahead of the staging probe that §7.1 says must settle the disputed causality first.

**Chapter 10 has no mechanism holding it shut at the widget layer.** `authority_basis: 'pre_authorized_presentation'` is an emitter-written literal with no binding to a pre-existing canonical artefact, while `WidgetSource` permits a fresh capability read and the moment list includes `growth_plan` and `marketing_broadcast` — so a scheduler can compose new strategy and label it pre-authorized. INV-11 permits DRAFT on proactive envelopes where the C10 guard and the IA both forbid it, and the contract nowhere forbids a proactive REFINE from opening a C9 run — which is precisely how the compatibility section describes the C10 loop in widget terms. The eventToken guard covers notifications, not the in-app greeting slot.

**"Required C9 contract changes: 0" does not survive the design's own taxonomy.** Four of its twenty-two kinds and five of the eight restorations need `consent.*`, `identity.*`, commerce-write and cross-runtime `cutmatch.*` keys that are not in the registry, while INV-10, §2.2 and §4.3 require every capability to be in it; P02's "strict superset" canon resolves the tension by breaking those three rules instead. I verified `C9_REGISTRY_HASH` is frozen over `C9_CAPABILITIES` with `c9Deny('registry_version_unavailable')` on mismatch, so registry growth is a versioned C9 event that also invalidates every persisted frozen-receipt envelope. Separately, `four_eyes` requires a change to `canDecide` (verified: `approvalPolicy: 'owner'` returns true for any OWNER_ROLE, initiator included) and the contract applies none of the seven corrections its own compatibility section declares mandatory — yet P03 freezes it.

**Parity is claimed beyond the gate's coverage, and the gate cannot be discharged.** The IA declares 112 → 5 with 107 entry points leaving primary navigation; the ledger has 63 retirement rows, 126 untriaged surfaces and a completion threshold of ≤ 49. The 76 fullscreen-detail rows lose their entry point and change their authorisation mechanism while bound by only G1/G2/G4. G9 demands 7/7 overlays against a census the design itself corrected to six. And P27 depends on P30 while P30 depends on every package above it — a literal cycle that makes the only deletion-permitting wave unenterable.

**Role removal reaches security in two places.** Preview fence 3 becomes "capability absence" because the tab is gone and fence 5 becomes a projector rule, putting both behind one emission-time decision that the independence mutation test and G5 explicitly forbid; and D1's recommended removal of the persona field would leave A4/INV-18 — the sixth PII fence — with a predicate that can never be true, since it is keyed on `presentation_mode === 'client'`.

**Chat-first slides toward chat-only in two capability classes.** The IA adopts D4-A against the decision record's recommendation, leaving 201 KEEP-AS-CAPABILITY surfaces reachable only by composing an utterance, with no chrome entry and no index; and FORM — the kind carrying cash declaration, expense correction and loyalty adjustment — has no mandated fallback editor in the contract and `partial_save: false`, while the taxonomy claims fullscreen is required for it.

The scope discipline in the individual sections is genuine and unusually explicit — each opens with the fence, and the platform and C9/C10 sections hold it well ("specified this cycle; not implemented this cycle"). What fails is coherence between them: the contract, the IA, the migration map, the packages plan and the decision record give different answers to when production may be touched, how many surfaces retire, what the proactive ceiling is, how many widget kinds exist, and whether the persona field survives. Every one of those disagreements resolves at implementation time in favour of the looser document.

"Required C9 contract changes: 0" (c9-c10-compat headline) — four of the taxonomy's kinds and five of the eight restorations require capability keys absent from the C9 registry, whose hash is frozen and carried in envelopes as capability_version.

"The greeting composer is denied the DRAFT, REQUEST_APPROVAL and COMMIT effect classes at emission time" (IA §8) — INV-11, the only invariant that binds proactive envelopes, permits DRAFT; no invariant implements the IA's prohibition.

"The only mechanism that may ever authorise a deletion is INV-16" (contract §0, §13; migration map §0; packages §1) — two deletions are authorised elsewhere with "no parity gate" and "immediately".

violations.why: The platform section's channel union is `pwa | native-shell | telegram-miniapp | telegram-bot | web-push | realtime-voice | guest-chat | web-public | public-community | sms | email` — 11 of the 17 evidenced channels. Missing: `scheduler` (32 surfaces), `smm-bot` (26), `edge-relay` (21), `backend` (7), `social-publishing` (7), `public-web-auth` (6) — 99 evidenced surfaces. The 7-tier table has no `NON_INTERACTIVE` tier at all, although `NON_INTERACTIVE` is a member of the contract's own `interaction_model` and is the target of ladder step 9. So the scheduler — a designated minter, and the carrier of all 12 proactive moments, all of which the inventory says any new chat UX must cover — has no registered profile, no tier and no fitting rule, and `G1 profile matrix` ("every envelope kind × 7 tiers") cannot cover the channel where proactive delivery actually happens.
violations.fix: Add the six missing channels to `ChannelId` and give `NON_INTERACTIVE` a tier row with `max_intents: 0`, `NAVIGATE/HANDOFF` ceiling and a mandatory text-equivalent-plus-signed-link rendering; extend G1 to `kinds × tiers` including it.

violations.constraint: Consent accept/decline is never a chat-rendered control actuated by channel identity alone; a widget may not promise a capability with no canonical owner (P2)
violations.where: section-migration-map.md §8 Tier B, `GAP-CONSENT-REGISTER-EXPORT` ("Restored to: a `REPORT` widget with a top-3 summary card and a mandatory `fullscreen_detail: compliance.consent_register` + `export_intent`, delivered as an artefact into the conversation") against contract.md §6.8 NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED (which lists `consent.register.export`) and section-widget-taxonomy.md §9 ("`ARTIFACT` is emittable only for owner reports; the consent-register export has no owner")
violations.why: Three internal contradictions on one row. (1) `consent.register.export` is on NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED, whose "only legal intent is HANDOFF" — yet the restoration home is a chat REPORT carrying an `export_intent` that delivers the Roskomnadzor journal into the transcript. That is precisely a chat-actuated control over a 152-FZ capability, and it also writes a register of identified data subjects into conversation history, which §8 Delete then makes erasable. (2) It relies on delivery "as an artefact", and ARTIFACT is not a kind the contract can express. (3) The taxonomy states this capability has no registered owner, so P2 forbids any intent at all until one exists — the migration map names an intent anyway. The gap ledger exists to prevent exactly this pattern (promising a remedy with no owner).
violations.fix: Restate the row as: a `LIMITATION` with `capability_gap_ref: GAP-CONSENT-REGISTER-EXPORT` and no intent until the owner is registered; thereafter a `HANDOFF`-only entry to `fullscreen_detail: compliance.consent_register` behind `SESSION_VERIFIED`+, with the file delivered on the verified surface and never into the chat transcript.

violations.constraint: No old screen deleted before proven capability parity — INV-16 is the only mechanism that may authorise a deletion
violations.where: contract.md §12 INV-16 ("Every KEEP-disposition capability in the 669-disposition inventory has ≥1 of: a widget kind, a fullscreen route, a text intent") against the evidenced disposition split and section-migration-map.md §3
violations.why: As worded in the primary artefact, INV-16 binds only KEEP-disposition rows. The evidenced inventory has two KEEP dispositions (KEEP AS CAPABILITY 201, KEEP AS FULLSCREEN DETAIL 76 = 277 rows). So the gate that §0 and §13 describe as "the only mechanism that may ever authorise a deletion" does not, as written, cover the rows that delete. The migration map's §3 gate is correct and per-row (RETIRE binds G1–G9 plus a named successor in `parity_proven_by`); the contract's one-line restatement of it is narrower than the thing it gates, and the contract is the artefact CI will be written from.
violations.fix: Rewrite INV-16 to bind every row whose terminal state removes an entry point or a surface — RETIRE, MOVE INTO CHAT WIDGET, MERGE — and to fail closed on any row whose disposition is UNTRIAGED, matching section-migration-map.md §3 and §1.5.

violations.constraint: No BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION; the free-input surface must be rationed and countable
violations.where: contract.md §5.2 B2 ("FORM is the only kind accepting free-form input and is therefore the designed leak; its emissions are counted per tenant per week") against contract.md:315 CHOICE body (`allow_free_text; free_text_hint?`) and §6.1 `InputSchema.fields.type` (`'string' | 'integer' | 'date' | 'time' | 'phone'` with only `max_len`/`pattern`)
violations.why: The claim that FORM is the *only* free-form kind is false against the contract's own CHOICE body, which carries `allow_free_text`, and against `InputSchema`, which permits unbounded-domain scalar types on an intent of any kind (only `enum` and `ref` carry `enum_values`). The consequence is not stylistic: the per-tenant FORM emission counter — the design's stated (social) control on the free-input surface — does not observe the CHOICE free-text path or any `string`/`phone`/`integer`/`date` input on a non-FORM kind, so the one metric the design offers for its acknowledged leak under-counts it by construction. Ladder step 4 also escalates multi-select chains into FORM, further mixing the population the counter is meant to bound.
violations.fix: Either remove `allow_free_text` from CHOICE (free text is a chat message, not a widget field) or extend the justification requirement and the emission counter to every envelope carrying a non-closed-domain input field, and say so in B2 instead of naming FORM as the only one.

verdict: VIOLATIONS FOUND — 24 findings, 16 STRUCTURAL. This pass reviewed only for unproven, overstated and uncheckable claims, and it both confirms and extends the prior safety review. Most of the design's repository-derived numbers are exact and I verified them: 795 surfaces / 17 channels / 669 dispositions / 126 untriaged / 112 primaryNav / 465 pwa / 32 scheduler; the disposition split 201/121/115/93/76/63; 291 distinct raw widgetType strings; the 12 proactive moments verbatim; the five client-preview enforcement points; the a11y baseline (458 onClick, 189 'button', 3 aria-live, 1 aria-expanded, 4 tabIndex, 25 aria-label, 14 reduced-motion blocks, 7 occurrences of zIndex 2147483000); 103 architecture specs; 47 app.module registrations; `database.mute_master` raising PermissionError. The taxonomy's correction of the brief is also correct: the registry resolves to 56 entries (47 MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG tools + 9 orchestration extras), not 57. The failures cluster in three places. First, the contract is not the version the design's own compatibility analysis passed: section-c9-c10-compat declares C9 PASS conditional on seven corrections and STRATEGY_OPTIONS FAIL as written, and contract.md applies almost none of them — so §4.3's claim to mirror AgentResult@1 field-for-field is verifiably false (facts_used drops the required evidence_refs and flattens c9Completeness to a number), `four_eyes` asserts an enforcement that returns zero grep hits in the backend and that ai-tool-policy's canDecide contradicts, `reversible: boolean` has no canonical source because C9's only value is the literal SOURCE_DEFINED, STRATEGY_OPTIONS does not reuse c9Alternative and INV-13 is unsatisfiable against c9.store's cap of three and c9.strategy.ts:135's truncation of NO_ACTION, and PROGRESS still carries 'failed' in a contract that claims no error severity exists anywhere in it. Second, the widget taxonomy and the contract publish two incompatible closed sets — 22 versus 17 — and the five missing kinds are precisely the ones carrying consent, identity, payment, generated media and file delivery; the taxonomy's own argument that CONSENT_STATE converts NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED "from a maintained list into a type rule" therefore has no expression in the delivered contract, and two registered capabilities (owner_report.status/download) still have no home. Third, the primary-navigation arithmetic is wrong and a completion gate is built on it: only 19 of the 63 RETIRE rows are primaryNav in the evidenced inventory, so executing every assigned retirement leaves 93 nav entries, not 49, while the IA simultaneously claims 107 of 112 leave and D2 remains an open owner decision. On the specific checks requested: all eight no-route capabilities DO have a named restoration home in the migration map, but two homes are defective — the consent-register export is routed as a chat-delivered artefact against its own NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED classification and an unexpressible kind, and the Telegram unbind restores only the offboarding half while identity.client.channel.unbind has no row at all. The accessibility contract (A11yFloor@1) is serious work and largely sound, but it does not cover every widget type: role_hint has no value for SCHEDULE, PROGRESS, REPORT, METRIC, BOOKING_CONFIRMATION, APPROVAL or SETTINGS_DRAFT, no clause defines a keyboard model outside radiogroup/listbox, no clause covers data-table semantics at all, reading_order is typed so that A-3 and INV-9 cannot be satisfied for at least eight kinds, the fullscreen detail whose declared reason is literally 'accessibility' is bound by no clause, and A-13's SC 2.2.1 discharge is contradicted by the contract's own 120-second BOOKING_CONFIRMATION ceiling with collapse-to-summary and no extension affordance. Every one of the seventeen brief-named kinds is present in the contract enum with a body, so that specific check passes; expressibility fails only for the taxonomy's five additions and for per-kind accessibility and reading-order typing.
